blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 2.1
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 2.1

blocks.text: BOOK II — ŚĀKTOPĀYA
blocks.directed: [long pause] BOOK II — ŚĀKTOPĀYA

blocks.text: चित्तं मन्त्रः
blocks.directed: [slowly] चित्तं मन्त्रः

blocks.text: Cittaṃ mantraḥ.
blocks.directed: Cittaṃ mantraḥ.

blocks.text: The mind is mantra.
blocks.directed: The mind is mantra.

blocks.text: Congratulations, Your Mind Is Now a Mantra.
blocks.directed: Congratulations, Your Mind Is Now a Mantra.

blocks.text: Ladies and gentlemen.
blocks.directed: Ladies and gentlemen.

blocks.text: He’s done it again.
blocks.directed: He’s done it again.

blocks.text: Two words.
blocks.directed: Two words.

blocks.text: Two bloody words.
blocks.directed: Two bloody words.

blocks.text: And the entire philosophy of mantra has just been turned upside down.
blocks.directed: And the entire philosophy of mantra has just been turned upside down.

blocks.text: Cittaṃ mantraḥ.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Cittaṃ mantraḥ.

blocks.text: The mind is mantra.
blocks.directed: The mind is mantra.

blocks.text: Now, hang on.
blocks.directed: Now, hang on.

blocks.text: Didn’t we just spend the entire first book explaining that ordinary cognition produces bondage?
blocks.directed: Didn’t we just spend the entire first book explaining that ordinary cognition produces bondage?

blocks.text: Wasn’t differentiated knowledge responsible for the whole miserable business of individual limitation?
blocks.directed: Wasn’t differentiated knowledge responsible for the whole miserable business of individual limitation?

blocks.text: And now we’re being told that the mind is a sacred instrument of liberation?
blocks.directed: And now we’re being told that the mind is a sacred instrument of liberation?

blocks.text: What’s going on?
blocks.directed: What’s going on?

blocks.text: Has Vasugupta forgotten what he wrote?
blocks.directed: Has Vasugupta forgotten what he wrote?

blocks.text: Has the manuscript been assembled in the wrong order?
blocks.directed: Has the manuscript been assembled in the wrong order?

blocks.text: Is Śiva having an administrative disagreement with himself?
blocks.directed: Is Śiva having an administrative disagreement with himself?

blocks.text: No.
blocks.directed: No.

blocks.text: This is the central brilliance of Śāktopāya.
blocks.directed: This is the central brilliance of Śāktopāya.

blocks.text: The same consciousness that appears contracted into ordinary mental activity can be recognised in its divine nature.
blocks.directed: The same consciousness that appears contracted into ordinary mental activity can be recognised in its divine nature.

blocks.text: But Kṣemarāja immediately makes an important qualification.
blocks.directed: But Kṣemarāja immediately makes an important qualification.

blocks.text: He isn’t saying every random mental fluctuation automatically functions as a liberating mantra.
blocks.directed: He isn’t saying every random mental fluctuation automatically functions as a liberating mantra.

blocks.text: Your thoughts about what to eat for dinner are not necessarily the supreme mantra.
blocks.directed: Your thoughts about what to eat for dinner are not necessarily the supreme mantra.

blocks.text: Neither is mentally rehearsing a conversation in which you absolutely destroy somebody who disagreed with you three years ago.
blocks.directed: Neither is mentally rehearsing a conversation in which you absolutely destroy somebody who disagreed with you three years ago.

blocks.text: Although, admittedly, that can feel rather powerful.
blocks.directed: Although, admittedly, that can feel rather powerful.

blocks.text: The relevant citta is consciousness actively engaged in contemplating the supreme reality.
blocks.directed: The relevant citta is consciousness actively engaged in contemplating the supreme reality.

blocks.text: Let’s take the Sanskrit apart.
blocks.directed: Let’s take the Sanskrit apart.

blocks.text: Cit — consciousness, awareness.
blocks.directed: Cit — consciousness, awareness.

blocks.text: Citta — mind or mental consciousness, particularly in its active, modified condition.
blocks.directed: Citta — mind or mental consciousness, particularly in its active, modified condition.

blocks.text: Mantra — a sacred formula, but also understood traditionally through the acts of contemplation and protection.
blocks.directed: Mantra — a sacred formula, but also understood traditionally through the acts of contemplation and protection.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja gives a characteristic tantric explanation connecting mantra with:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Kṣemarāja gives a characteristic tantric explanation connecting mantra with:

blocks.text: Manana — inward contemplation.
blocks.directed: Manana — inward contemplation.

blocks.text: Trāṇa — protection or deliverance.
blocks.directed: Trāṇa — protection or deliverance.

blocks.text: This is a traditional interpretive derivation, not a claim that the two words mechanically combine according to ordinary Sanskrit morphology.
blocks.directed: This is a traditional interpretive derivation, not a claim that the two words mechanically combine according to ordinary Sanskrit morphology.

blocks.text: But the philosophical meaning is fantastic.
blocks.directed: But the philosophical meaning is fantastic.

blocks.text: The mantra is that through which contemplation becomes liberating.
blocks.directed: The mantra is that through which contemplation becomes liberating.

blocks.text: Liberating from what?
blocks.directed: Liberating from what?

blocks.text: From the fundamental misidentification that makes you experience yourself as a finite subject surrounded by an entirely separate world.
blocks.directed: From the fundamental misidentification that makes you experience yourself as a finite subject surrounded by an entirely separate world.

blocks.text: Here’s the really important bit.
blocks.directed: Here’s the really important bit.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja insists that the efficacy of mantra does not ultimately reside in an arrangement of letters considered separately from consciousness.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja insists that the efficacy of mantra does not ultimately reside in an arrangement of letters considered separately from consciousness.

blocks.text: The living power of mantra is realised through identification with the conscious reality of its deity.
blocks.directed: The living power of mantra is realised through identification with the conscious reality of its deity.

blocks.text: And this is an absolutely enormous claim.
blocks.directed: And this is an absolutely enormous claim.

blocks.text: Imagine chanting:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Imagine chanting:

blocks.text: ॐ नमः शिवाय।.
blocks.directed: [slowly] ॐ नमः शिवाय।.

blocks.text: Oṃ namaḥ śivāya.
blocks.directed: Oṃ namaḥ śivāya.

blocks.text: You can pronounce those sounds mechanically.
blocks.directed: You can pronounce those sounds mechanically.

blocks.text: You can repeat them while making breakfast.
blocks.directed: You can repeat them while making breakfast.

blocks.text: You can count them on a string of beads.
blocks.directed: You can count them on a string of beads.

blocks.text: You can construct an exceptionally complicated spreadsheet documenting your progress.
blocks.directed: You can construct an exceptionally complicated spreadsheet documenting your progress.

blocks.text: Very impressive.
blocks.directed: Very impressive.

blocks.text: Ten thousand repetitions.
blocks.directed: Ten thousand repetitions.

blocks.text: Beautiful chart.
blocks.directed: Beautiful chart.

blocks.text: Excellent consistency.
blocks.directed: Excellent consistency.

blocks.text: But what if your fundamental understanding remains:
blocks.directed: [short pause] But what if your fundamental understanding remains:

blocks.text: “I am a small individual over here, desperately attempting to contact a distant divine being over there”?
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am a small individual over here, desperately attempting to contact a distant divine being over there”?

blocks.text: Then the deepest nondual meaning of the mantra has not yet been recognised.
blocks.directed: Then the deepest nondual meaning of the mantra has not yet been recognised.

blocks.text: For Kṣemarāja, the culmination involves recognising the non-separation of the practitioner, mantra and deity.
blocks.directed: For Kṣemarāja, the culmination involves recognising the non-separation of the practitioner, mantra and deity.

blocks.text: The sound is not merely sent towards Śiva.
blocks.directed: The sound is not merely sent towards Śiva.

blocks.text: The very awareness in which the mantra appears is recognised as Śiva’s own conscious power.
blocks.directed: The very awareness in which the mantra appears is recognised as Śiva’s own conscious power.

blocks.text: That’s the transformation.
blocks.directed: That’s the transformation.

blocks.text: And notice how this relates to the previous book.
blocks.directed: And notice how this relates to the previous book.
[short pause] At 1.4:

blocks.text: ज्ञानाधिष्ठानं मातृका।.
blocks.directed: [slowly] ज्ञानाधिष्ठानं मातृका।.

blocks.text: Jñānādhiṣṭhānaṃ mātṛkā.
blocks.directed: Jñānādhiṣṭhānaṃ mātṛkā.

blocks.text: Mātṛkā is the foundation of differentiated knowledge.
blocks.directed: Mātṛkā is the foundation of differentiated knowledge.

blocks.text: Language participates in the structure of limitation.
blocks.directed: Language participates in the structure of limitation.

blocks.text: But now:
blocks.directed: [short pause] But now:

blocks.text: चित्तं मन्त्रः।.
blocks.directed: [slowly] चित्तं मन्त्रः।.

blocks.text: Cittaṃ mantraḥ.
blocks.directed: Cittaṃ mantraḥ.

blocks.text: The mind itself becomes mantra when its activity is directed towards recognition of its supreme source.
blocks.directed: The mind itself becomes mantra when its activity is directed towards recognition of its supreme source.

blocks.text: The problem was never that consciousness possessed the ability to articulate experience.
blocks.directed: The problem was never that consciousness possessed the ability to articulate experience.

blocks.text: The problem was the failure to recognise the true nature of that articulation.
blocks.directed: The problem was the failure to recognise the true nature of that articulation.

blocks.text: The same Śakti binds.
blocks.directed: The same Śakti binds.

blocks.text: The same Śakti liberates.
blocks.directed: The same Śakti liberates.

blocks.text: An extraordinary business model.
blocks.directed: An extraordinary business model.

blocks.text: She’s manufacturing the locks and distributing the keys.
blocks.directed: She’s manufacturing the locks and distributing the keys.

blocks.text: And the keys, apparently, were made from the same material as the locks.
blocks.directed: And the keys, apparently, were made from the same material as the locks.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja’s point: The mantra’s highest power is not mere pronunciation but contemplative identification with the divine consciousness embodied in it. He supports this reading with tantric scriptural passages and the Spandakārikā. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja’s point: The mantra’s highest power is not mere pronunciation but contemplative identification with the divine consciousness embodied in it. He supports this reading with tantric scriptural passages and the Spandakārikā. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Book II: Śāktopāya — The Way of Śakti.
blocks.directed: Book II: Śāktopāya — The Way of Śakti.

blocks.text: How to Turn Your Own Mind into a Divine Weapon, Discover That the Alphabet Is Literally a Goddess, and Finally Stop Being Such a Cosmically Confused Little Bastard.
blocks.directed: How to Turn Your Own Mind into a Divine Weapon, Discover That the Alphabet Is Literally a Goddess, and Finally Stop Being Such a Cosmically Confused Little Bastard.

blocks.text:
Previously, on the Śiva Sūtras…
Right.
blocks.directed:
Previously, on the Śiva Sūtras…
Right.

blocks.text: When we last encountered our spiritual protagonist Vasugupta, he’d made twenty-two rather explosive statements about the nature of reality.
blocks.directed: When we last encountered our spiritual protagonist Vasugupta, he’d made twenty-two rather explosive statements about the nature of reality.

blocks.text: We discovered that consciousness is the Self.
blocks.directed: We discovered that consciousness is the Self.

blocks.text: That limited knowledge is bondage.
blocks.directed: That limited knowledge is bondage.

blocks.text: That the entire universe is the body of Śiva.
blocks.directed: That the entire universe is the body of Śiva.

blocks.text: That enlightenment involves an extraordinary sense of wonder.
blocks.directed: That enlightenment involves an extraordinary sense of wonder.

blocks.text: And that, under certain rather ambitious tantric interpretations, a sufficiently accomplished yogi may possess supernatural powers.
blocks.directed: And that, under certain rather ambitious tantric interpretations, a sufficiently accomplished yogi may possess supernatural powers.

blocks.text: All perfectly reasonable.
blocks.directed: All perfectly reasonable.

blocks.text: But then Vasugupta ended the first book with something particularly intriguing.
blocks.directed: But then Vasugupta ended the first book with something particularly intriguing.

blocks.text: महाह्रदानुसन्धानान्मन्त्रवीर्यानुभवः।.
blocks.directed: [slowly] महाह्रदानुसन्धानान्मन्त्रवीर्यानुभवः।.

blocks.text: Mahāhradānusandhānān mantravīryānubhavaḥ.
blocks.directed: Mahāhradānusandhānān mantravīryānubhavaḥ.

blocks.text: Through union with the Great Lake comes the experience of the potency of mantra.
blocks.directed: Through union with the Great Lake comes the experience of the potency of mantra.

blocks.text: The Great Lake.
blocks.directed: The Great Lake.

blocks.text: The unfathomable reservoir of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The unfathomable reservoir of consciousness.

blocks.text: The divine source of every sound, every thought, every manifestation.
blocks.directed: The divine source of every sound, every thought, every manifestation.

blocks.text: And now, naturally, we’ve got a question.
blocks.directed: And now, naturally, we’ve got a question.

blocks.text: If the power of mantra comes from consciousness…
blocks.directed: If the power of mantra comes from consciousness…

blocks.text: What the bloody hell actually is a mantra?
blocks.directed: What the bloody hell actually is a mantra?

blocks.text: Is it a magic word?
blocks.directed: Is it a magic word?

blocks.text: A sequence of Sanskrit syllables?
blocks.directed: A sequence of Sanskrit syllables?

blocks.text: A cosmic password?
blocks.directed: A cosmic password?

blocks.text: Does Śiva have some sort of metaphysical voice-recognition software?
blocks.directed: Does Śiva have some sort of metaphysical voice-recognition software?

blocks.text: Do you chant Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya fourteen thousand times and suddenly receive administrative privileges over the universe?
blocks.directed: Do you chant Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya fourteen thousand times and suddenly receive administrative privileges over the universe?

blocks.text: Well.
blocks.directed: Well.

blocks.text: Vasugupta is about to disappoint everyone who’s purchased a very expensive singing bowl.
blocks.directed: Vasugupta is about to disappoint everyone who’s purchased a very expensive singing bowl.

blocks.text: Because the answer is considerably more interesting.
blocks.directed: Because the answer is considerably more interesting.

blocks.text: Welcome to Śāktopāya.
blocks.directed: Welcome to Śāktopāya.

blocks.text: The way of Śakti.
blocks.directed: The way of Śakti.

blocks.text: Whereas Śāmbhavopāya centres on the immediate upsurge of recognition through divine will, Śāktopāya works through the power of awareness, understanding, contemplation and the transformation of cognition.
blocks.directed: Whereas Śāmbhavopāya centres on the immediate upsurge of recognition through divine will, Śāktopāya works through the power of awareness, understanding, contemplation and the transformation of cognition.

blocks.text: It’s not merely thinking about Śiva.
blocks.directed: It’s not merely thinking about Śiva.

blocks.text: It’s discovering what thinking actually is when illuminated by its own conscious source.
blocks.directed: It’s discovering what thinking actually is when illuminated by its own conscious source.

blocks.text: And this is where Kṣemarāja, writing his Śivasūtravimarśinī, really gets going.
blocks.directed: And this is where Kṣemarāja, writing his Śivasūtravimarśinī, really gets going.

blocks.text: Ten sūtras.
blocks.directed: Ten sūtras.

blocks.text: One extraordinarily sophisticated theory of mantra, language, consciousness and liberation.
blocks.directed: One extraordinarily sophisticated theory of mantra, language, consciousness and liberation.

blocks.text: All ten Sanskrit formulations below follow the traditional Śāktopāya sequence; the explanations follow Kṣemarāja rather than treating the brief aphorisms as self-explanatory.
blocks.directed: All ten Sanskrit formulations below follow the traditional Śāktopāya sequence; the explanations follow Kṣemarāja rather than treating the brief aphorisms as self-explanatory.
